source_caption:
When Martin Scorsese cast legendary director Rob Reiner to play Jordan Belfort’s deeply explosive, perpetually enraged father “Mad Max,” he gave the comedy veteran completely free rein to let loose. Reiner improvised nearly all of his hilariously terrifying, expletive-laden rants. His ferocious, wildly unhinged delivery was so intensely funny that Leonardo DiCaprio and Jonah Hill desperately struggled to stay in character, and Scorsese himself ruined several takes by laughing uncontrollably behind the monitor. By letting a legendary filmmaker completely unleash his own comedic chaos on set, Scorsese masterfully proves that the most memorable, scene-stealing cinematic moments often happen when you simply point a camera at a comedic genius and let them entirely off the leash.
⠀
The Wolf of Wall Street (2013), directed by Martin Scorsese, starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Jonah Hill, Margot Robbie. A fiercely ambitious, deeply corrupt New York stockbroker orchestrates a wildly illegal, massively lucrative penny-stock boiler room, plunging into a profoundly chaotic, drug-fueled life of absolute excess before his sprawling financial empire inevitably draws the relentless attention of the FBI.

source_details.title: The Wolf of Wall Street
source_details.synopsis: The Wolf of Wall Street is a 2013 American biographical film co-produced and directed by Martin Scorsese, written by Terence Winter, and based on Jordan Belfort's 2007 memoir. It loosely recounts Belfort's career as a stockbroker in New York City and how his firm, Stratton Oakmont, engaged in rampant corruption and fraud on Wall Street, leading to his downfall. The film stars Leonardo DiCaprio as Belfort; Jonah Hill as his business partner and friend Donnie Azoff; Margot Robbie as his second wife, Naomi Lapaglia; Matthew McConaughey as his mentor and former boss Mark Hanna; and Kyle Chandler as FBI special agent Patrick Denham portraying Gregory Coleman. It is DiCaprio's fifth collaboration
